extracted.intended_audience: IP practitioners, agents, and applicants in Malaysia (trademarks, GIs, industrial designs, layout-designs, copyright)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical legal standards and procedural requirements for filing, examination, opposition, registration, enforcement, and maintenance of Malaysian IP rights (trademarks, geographical indications, industrial designs, integrated circuit layout-designs, and copyright).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum documentation requirements for filing a trademark application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One clear specimen of the trademark in JPEG format (or relevant graphical/material representation for non-traditional marks); a list of goods/services (Nice Classification) in Word format; full name and street address of applicant (and state of incorporation where applicable); priority application number/date/country (if applicable); indicate language, English translation and transliteration for non-Roman/non-English characters (translation document not required). No power of attorney or statutory declaration required, but agent must make Declaration in application form confirming bona fides and entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classes and series filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowances for filing multiple classes and series of trademarks in one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple classes may be designated within a single application; applications may be divided or merged. A series application may include up to six representations resembling each other in material particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Application date is the filing date in Malaysia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application date of a trademark in Malaysia is its filing date, regardless of any Paris Convention priority claimed; priority date is used only for determining precedence during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited examination eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria limiting availability of expedited examination under TMA 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedited examination is possible but not available for certification and collective marks and most non-traditional marks (colour, sound, scent, hologram, positioning, sequence of motion). Grounds for expedited examination reduced to: (i) national or public interest; (ii) ongoing infringement proceedings or evidence of potential infringement; (iii) registration required to obtain monetary benefits from government/institutions recognized by the Registrar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination scope and search
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar's examination powers and the scope of searches during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registrar shall carry out examination of an application, including a search of earlier or well-known trademarks (relative grounds under Section 24), and as considered necessary; substantive objections may be raised despite lack of full substantive exam process elsewhere in the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal (Section 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of marks that shall be refused by the Registrar under absolute grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks devoid of distinctive character; marks consisting exclusively of signs serving in trade to designate kind/quality/purpose/value/geographical origin/other characteristics; signs consisting exclusively of a shape resulting from the nature of the goods, necessary to obtain a technical result, or giving substantial value; trademarks likely to deceive or mislead the public as to nature/quality/geographical origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-strike provisional refusal rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant allowed a single substantive response to a provisional refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has one opportunity to make representations, amend, or furnish evidence within the period specified in the Registrar's written notice. If the Registrar maintains refusal after that one submission, a total provisional refusal issues and the applicant must appeal to the High Court for further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Stages and statutory timing of opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition begins with opponent filing grounds and notice within two months of publication. Applicant files counter-statement within two months of receipt. Opponent then files evidence by statutory declaration within two months; applicant replies with statutory declaration two months later; opponent may file evidence-in-reply strictly in reply. No further evidence except by leave. Upon completion, Registrar requests written submissions and may refuse register or register subject to conditions; decision appealable to High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar control of extensions and service proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on extensions and service evidence requirements in opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar strictly controls extension lengths to minimize delay/abuse. Parties must file an affidavit of service to the Registrar within 14 days of serving relevant documents to the other party to avoid miscommunication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation by successor-in-title and deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation rights and deferral of opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition may be continued by a successor-in-title to the trademark; the Registrar can defer proceedings upon request if prescribed circumstances are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration effects and certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: What is issued upon successful registration and presumption of validity timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon successful registration, a sealed notification is issued; a certificate of registration may be requested for a prescribed fee. Presumption that a registration is valid and conclusive generally arises five years after registration (with exceptions). Renewal of multiple-class registrations can be selective; classes not renewed must be removed by division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording transfers and priority of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of recording assignments, security interests and other transactions with MyIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments, security interests, charges or court-ordered transfers are not enforceable against another conflicting interest unless recorded with MyIPO. Trademark licences are not statutorily required to be registered to be effective, but if recorded, the public is deemed to have notice of the licence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark licences formalities and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements and recognition of exclusive and non-exclusive licences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licences are effective if in writing and signed by the licensor. Exclusive licences and sub-licensing are expressly recognised; exclusive licensee rights are distinct from non-exclusive. Courts may take losses suffered by a licensee into account in infringement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation and invalidation grounds (removal from register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances where a registration may be revoked or invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may revoke within 12 months from registration if it was a wrongful grant. Court may revoke registration (on application) under prescribed circumstances including three years of non-use from notification of registration or suspended use for continuous three years without proper reasons. Registration may be invalidated for absolute/relative grounds, fraud or misrepresentation in procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement: registered vs unregistered marks and passing off
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection available to registered and unregistered trademarks and interplay with passing off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both registered and unregistered trademarks are protected; most enforcement litigated in IP-specialised High Court. Unregistered marks are protected under common law passing off. Registrar must refuse registration under relative grounds if use is prevented by law protecting an unregistered mark or other sign used in trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of trademark infringement and secondary liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanded scope of infringement and liability for secondary users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement may arise from use of a similar (not necessarily identical) mark on similar goods/services. Liability may extend to secondary users who know or have reasons to believe such use is unauthorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionability of threats regarding infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Threats of infringement without basis are actionable offences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is an actionable offence to threaten infringement without basis. A mere notification that a trademark is registered does not constitute a threat. Aggrieved persons may seek declaration that threats are unjustified, damages, and injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfeit enforcement standard and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Porting of counterfeit offences and evidentiary role of Registrar verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many criminal offences and penalties under the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 were ported to TMA 2019. No need to obtain a Trade Description Order to act against a counterfeit not identical to the registered mark; Registrar's verification of confusing similarities is prima facie evidence in such proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication (GI) definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a GI and the kinds of products it covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A GI identifies goods as originating from a particular territory/region/locality where a given quality, reputation or characteristics is attributable to that geographical origin; applies to natural/agricultural products as well as industrial products and handicrafts. Governed by the Geographical Indications Act 2000 and Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI qualification exclusions (Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: GIs that may not qualify for protection in Malaysia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GIs contrary to public order or morality; GIs that have ceased to be protected in the country/territory of origin; GIs that have fallen into disuse in the country/territory of origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI application process and applicant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may apply for a GI and required application information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rightful applicant: a producer, a competent authority, or trade organisation/association. Foreign applicants must appoint a Malaysia-based agent as address for service. Required information: identification and capacity of applicant, the GI and goods, statutory declaration of bona fides, summary of characteristics/quality, geographical map and supporting documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI opposition timing and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition period and possible grounds to oppose a GI registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month statutory period from advertisement date to oppose. Grounds include the Section 4 exemptions (public order/morality, ceased protection or disuse in origin) and other valid reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI registration term and use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of GI registration and limits on who may use the registered GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GI registration valid and enforceable for 10 years from application date, renewable indefinitely; Registrar may require particulars on renewal to ensure GI not fallen into disuse. Only producers carrying on stipulated activities in the specified geographical area may use the registered GI in accordance with the quality, reputation and characteristics specified in the Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI remedies for unlawful use
rubrics_metrics.description: Available remedies for unlawful use of a GI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons may bring court proceedings for injunction, damages or other remedies against unlawful use, including misleading use as to geographical origin or acts of unfair competition under Article 10bis of the Paris Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrable industrial design definition
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes an industrial design for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features of shape, configuration, pattern or ornament applied to an article by any industrial process, judged by the eye in the finished article. 'Article' includes any article of manufacture or handicraft or part made and sold separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-registrable industrial design features
rubrics_metrics.description: List of items excluded from registration under Malaysian industrial design law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method or principle of construction; features dictated solely by function; features dependent on the appearance of another article of which it forms an integral part; integrated circuits (protected elsewhere); designs contrary to public order and morality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of design protection (visual appearance and single appearance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations on what is protected and how many appearances may be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection is for the external visual appearance of the article as a whole. Not possible to protect more than a single external visual appearance; patent-type claims/descriptions attempting to claim multiple appearances are impermissible. Cannot register part of an article unless that part is normally made and sold separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design novelty standard (since 01 July 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty requirement for industrial designs (worldwide vs local standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 01 July 2013, worldwide novelty: design must not have been disclosed to the public anywhere before priority date/application date with respect to the same or any other article. Identical or similar disclosures in domestic applications with earlier priority that proceeded to registration can defeat novelty. Publication in official/exhibitions or unlawful disclosure by a third person within six months prior to filing may be excluded from novelty-destroying disclosures. Degree of newness: not new if differing only in 'immaterial details' or 'features commonly used in the relevant trade'. Pre-01 July 2013 registrations are subject to local novelty (prior disclosure in Malaysia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of novelty requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Content and form guidance for the statement of novelty in design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include a statement of novelty, typically 'the novelty resides in the features of shape and configuration of the article as shown in the representations' or analogous wording for pattern/ornament. If highlighting a particular feature, indicate it (e.g., 'as shown in solid line'). Avoid patent-type claims or descriptions; registrations are generally for whole articles but novelty residing in part may be reflected in the statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple industrial design application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How multiple design applications are filed and treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple design applications permitted where designs belong to same Locarno class. Different authors and priority claims allowed but the applicant must be the same. Each design is protected separately and treated as a separate application during prosecution and registration; separate fees and separate registration numbers/certificates are allocated for each design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set of articles definition and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single application may cover a set of articles and scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Set of articles' = articles of same general character ordinarily sold together or used together, with the same industrial design applied to each. Each article of a set is protected separately; infringement need not copy the complete set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and particulars required for an industrial design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant name/address/state of incorporation/nationality; Appointment of Agent Form (ID Form 10) signed by applicant (no notarization/legalization required); full name and address of author; how applicant derived rights from author (assignment/employment/agreement); one set of representations (drawings/photos, each ≤12.5cm by 9cm); statement of novelty; name of article; class/sub-class of International Design Classification; designation of view(s) to be published; details of priority claim; priority document and certified English translation. If Appointment of Agent form unavailable, extension requested or certified copy may be submitted with original later. Drawings preferable to photographs to avoid formality objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design application procedure and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing steps, formal checks and absence of routine substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications assigned a design application number and filing date and checked for formal requirement compliance. There is no search or substantive examination as a matter of course, though substantive objections (e.g., as to whether a design falls within legal definition) may be raised. For multiple design applications, amendments and fees must be filed/paid separately per design. If not completed within 12 months due to applicant default, application deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design duration, renewal and late payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Term of protection and renewal regime for industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial term 5 years from filing date (MyIPO uses priority date in practice). Renewable for four further five-year periods for a maximum of 25 years. Renewal fee may be paid anytime prior to expiry; late payment allowed up to six months after expiry subject to penalty fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed design registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and timing for restoring an unintentionally lapsed registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may apply for restoration within one year of publication of notice of lapsing in Official Journal if failure to renew was due to accident or mistake. Interested parties may oppose proposed restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: UK registered designs continuation in Malaysia
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of pre-1999 UK registered designs in Malaysia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UK registered designs granted and in force prior to 01 Sep 1999 can be maintained in Malaysia via renewal applications; renewals due at 5-year periods from priority date. Since 15 Feb 2012, renewal for fourth/fifth 5-year period subject to official fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design infringement acts and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts that constitute infringement and limitation period for proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without licence/consent, infringement includes applying registered design (or fraudulent/obvious imitation) to any article for which design is registered; importing such articles into Malaysia for sale or trade; selling/stocking/hiring such articles. Infringement proceedings must be taken within five years of the infringing act(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation grounds for registered designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds upon which an industrial design registration may be revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person may apply to High Court for revocation where the design is not new or registration was procured by unlawful means. Provisions exist for rectification of the Register by aggrieved persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated circuit layout-designs: definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Key statutory definitions for integrated circuits and layout-designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Integrated circuit' = product (final or intermediate) with integrally formed elements and interconnections intended to perform an electronic function. 'Layout-design' = three-dimensional disposition of elements and interconnections of an integrated circuit or such disposition prepared for manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification for automatic protection of layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions required for automatic protection of layout-designs (no registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection automatic if: (i) layout-design is original (result of creator's own intellectual effort and not commonplace at creation); (ii) layout-design fixed in material form (including storable forms) or incorporated into an integrated circuit; (iii) right holder was a qualifying person at time of creation. 'Qualifying person' defined by nationality, domicile/residence, incorporation, or effective industrial/commercial establishment in Malaysia or WTO member country (including governments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for layout-designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration rules for layout-design protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected for 10 years from first commercial exploitation anywhere in the world, but not to exceed 15 years from creation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by layout-design protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive rights granted to right holders of layout-designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right holder may reproduce or authorize reproduction of all or a substantial part of protected layout-design (by incorporation or otherwise) and commercially exploit or authorize commercial exploitation of the protected layout-design, integrated circuits containing it, or articles containing such integrated circuits (commercial exploitation includes selling, letting for hire, distributing and importation for these purposes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design infringement and innocent user defence
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes infringement and the innocent defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally infringement to do listed acts in Malaysia without consent. No infringement where act done innocently—i.e., the person did not know and could not reasonably be expected to have known that a copy of the protected layout-design or integrated circuit/article was unauthorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout-design enforcement remedies and presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Judicial remedies and evidentiary presumption in enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right holder may bring action in High Court; Court may grant injunction, damages, account of profits or other relief. No damages against a defendant unaware and without grounds for suspecting infringement at time of act. Unless defendant puts matter in issue, presumption that layout-design is protected and plaintiff is right holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright categories and protection scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of works protected and basis of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories include literary, artistic and musical works; examples: books, manuals, songs, drawings, sculptures, films, sound recordings, computer source code. Protection is for form of expression in material form, regardless of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright qualification tests (Section 10 interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways a work may qualify for copyright protection in Malaysia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status of Author: author must be citizen or permanent resident of Malaysia or of any Berne Convention member country at time work made. First Publication: work must be first made available to public in Malaysia or any Berne Convention country; if first made available elsewhere, must be made available within 30 days to Malaysia or a Berne country. Place of Making: works (other than published editions) must be made in Malaysia, or (other than sound recordings, broadcasts and published editions) made in any Berne country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership defaults and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Who initially owns copyright and circumstances where ownership differs from author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule: author is copyright owner. Exceptions: commissioned works or works created in course of employment—copyright vests in commissioner or employer, subject to any contrary agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsistence and proof of copyright (documentation and affidavit)
rubrics_metrics.description: How protection arises and evidentiary measures to prove ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection conferred as-of-right to original work produced with sufficient skill and effort and expressed in material form. Formal registration not mandatory but advisable to document creation and ownership (e.g., © notice). Section 42 allows an affidavit/statutory declaration asserting copyright subsists in annexed true copy and that declarant is owner; facts in affidavit may be used as prima facie evidence in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary notification (recording with MyIPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional recording of copyright claims and requirements for notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Copyright (Voluntary Notification) Regulations 2012 and Section 26A, author/owner/assignee/licensee (or representative for non-residents) may notify Copyright Controller and deposit a copy of eligible work for recording in Register. Notification requires particulars of owner/author, statutory declaration of locus standi, a copy of the work, date/place of first publication, prescribed fee; translations required if not in national language or English. Controller does not verify claims; accuracy depends on applicant. Submitted copy must be clear and durable; hard or electronic copies permitted. Registered notification certificate (for fee) is prima facie evidence in Malaysian courts.
